findings.message: The diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (image scripts, lib, k8s, skills, README) but bumps no version. No plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json or .claude-plugin/marketplace.json entry appears in it. Bump every plugin's .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json and every marketplace.json plugins[] entry to the same new version.
findings.scenario: This change merges with all manifests still at the old version -> the CI version-sync check fails, or a released plugin ships new behaviour under the old version number.

findings.message: When save_bundle fails (no new commits, disk full, unwritable dir), it reports bundle=none but leaves any older work.bundle in place. mv and the work.base write are also two separate steps, so a failure between them leaves a new bundle with an old base. Remove the old pair when a new save fails, or write both files to temp names and rename them together.
findings.scenario: Run 1 saves bundle A. Run 2 resumes from A, adds commits, the push fails, and bundle create fails -> the record says bundle=none, but the next --retry silently resumes from the older A and drops run 2's commits.

findings.message: bundle_subpath keeps only the last 3 URL path segments and pads with only the host's first label. Different repos can then map to the same subPath and share a bundle folder.
findings.scenario: https://github.com/o/r and https://github.example.com/o/r (change 049-x) both give github/o/r/049-x. Likewise gitlab a/b/c/d and x/b/c/d collide. One repo's run could resume from the other's bundle (the base-ancestor check is the only guard).

findings.message: With several nodes, check_bundles passes whenever node_label is non-empty. It never checks that the label matches exactly one node, so doctor can say ok when the ReadWriteOnce claim cannot be mounted everywhere.
findings.scenario: node_label matches 2 nodes and the claim is bound to node a -> doctor prints 'ok bundles', but a Job scheduled on node b cannot mount the claim and hangs until the deadline.

findings.message: The read-only-folder case relies on chmod a-w. When the test runs as root (common in CI containers), `-w` is still true and the case does not exercise the read-only path. Skip the case or mark it unknown when id -u is 0.
findings.scenario: CI runs as root -> save_bundle writes the bundle, bundle=saved is recorded, and the no_folder check fails or the case proves nothing.

findings.message: The namespace is hard-coded to specclaw-fleet, but `namespace` is configurable and doctor looks in D_NS. The default /fleet/bundles and the default of 4 attempts are also written in several places (tracker.sh twice, workspace.sh, podspec.sh). Document that the namespace must be edited, or apply with -n.
findings.scenario: fleet.namespace=other -> `kubectl apply -f bundles-pvc.yaml` creates the claim in specclaw-fleet, and doctor reports 'claim not found' with the same apply hint.
